title: Add blog category filter and full-text search on /blog page using Fuse.js
description: Implement client-side search and category filtering for blog posts using Fuse.js to improve long-tail SEO and user discoverability. Filter by category (JB Guide, Singapore, Gig Work, Visa Info) and search by post title/excerpt with fuzzy matching. Update URL with query parameters for shareable search results.
acceptanceCriteria: Blog category dropdown filters posts by JB Guide, Singapore, Gig Work, Visa Info categories with post count badges
Fuse.js search indexes blog post title, excerpt, and author with fuzzy matching; displays results count on search
URL updates with ?search=query&category=value params; filter persists on page reload
technicalNotes: File to create: site/src/components/BlogSearch.tsx (~140 lines with Fuse.js indexing)
File to edit: site/src/app/blog/page.tsx (integrate BlogSearch component)
File to edit: site/src/data/blog/posts.ts (ensure all posts have category field)
Install: npm install fuse.js
Test command: npm run test -- blog-search.test.ts
Use Fuse.js indexOptions: { keys: ['title', 'excerpt', 'author'], threshold: 0.3 }

title: Write "Getting Around JB Without a Car — Transport Guide for Backpackers" blog post with cost breakdown
description: Publish new 1800+ word blog article targeting backpackers arriving in Johor Bahru without private transport. Include practical transport options (Johor Bus, MRT feeder, Grab, walking tours) with RM-per-trip costs, neighborhood walkability ratings, and internal links to related posts for SEO.
acceptanceCriteria: Blog post is 1800+ words covering Johor Bus routes (RM1-2), Grab usage (avg RM8 in-city), MRT feeder (RM1.50), walking neighborhoods (Little India, Taman Sentosa) with estimated costs per trip
Post includes rendered cost comparison table (transport type, avg cost, coverage area) and neighborhood walkability scores (1-5 stars)
Post includes internal links to '3-Day JB Backpacker Itinerary Under RM250' and 'Singapore RTS Link Guide' with proper schema.org IsSimilarTo markup
technicalNotes: File to create: post object in site/src/data/blog/posts.ts with slug 'jb-transport-guide', category 'JB Guide', published: true
Post must include: title, excerpt (<160 chars), author, date, featured image path in site/public/blog/
Test command: npm run test -- blog-content.test.ts -t "transport-guide"
Validate: wordCount > 1800, excerpt under 160 chars, relatedPosts array contains valid post slugs, images load

title: Create RelatedPosts component with automatic category-based linking for blog articles
description: Build a reusable RelatedPosts component that automatically fetches and displays 3 blog posts from the same category as the current article. Include schema.org IsSimilarTo markup, render on blog post layout, and ensure related posts are published and distinct from current post.
acceptanceCriteria: Component accepts currentPostId (slug), filters by category, and displays 3 published related posts excluding current post as ArticleCard components
Each related post card shows: title, author, publish date, excerpt, featured image, reading time, and category tag
Blog post layout.tsx renders RelatedPosts below article content with proper BreadcrumbList + IsSimilarTo schema.org JSON-LD
technicalNotes: File to create: site/src/components/RelatedPosts.tsx (~90 lines, exports RelatedPosts component)
File to edit: site/src/app/blog/[slug]/layout.tsx (add <RelatedPosts slug={slug} /> before </article>)
File to edit: site/src/lib/schema.ts (add generateIsSimilarToSchema function)
Test command: npm run test -- related-posts.test.ts
Filter logic: posts.filter(p => p.category === current.category && p.slug !== slug && p.published).slice(0, 3)

title: Add dynamic breadcrumb navigation with BreadcrumbList schema to blog and guide pages
description: Implement a reusable BreadcrumbNav component that renders breadcrumb trails for blog posts and guide sections with proper schema.org BreadcrumbList JSON-LD markup. Support mobile-responsive truncation and dynamic breadcrumb generation from pathname.
acceptanceCriteria: BreadcrumbNav renders trail: Home > Blog > Category > Post Title (blog) or Home > Guide > Section > Subsection (guide) with clickable links to parent pages
Component generates valid BreadcrumbList JSON-LD with @context, @type, and itemListElement containing @id, name, and position for each breadcrumb item
Mobile view truncates breadcrumb to Home > Current Page with tooltip showing full path; CSS matches hostel branding
technicalNotes: File to create: site/src/components/BreadcrumbNav.tsx (~120 lines, accepts items: BreadcrumbItem[] and renders <nav> with <ol>)
File to create: site/src/lib/breadcrumb.ts (~60 lines, exports getBreadcrumbs(pathname: string): BreadcrumbItem[])
File to edit: site/src/app/blog/[slug]/layout.tsx (add <BreadcrumbNav items={getBreadcrumbs(pathname)} /> in <header>)
Test command: npm run test -- breadcrumb.test.ts
JSON-LD: render as <script type='application/ld+json'>{"@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "BreadcrumbList", ...}</script>

title: Implement blog post reading time and word count metrics in post metadata and display
description: Create reading time calculation utility (200 wpm baseline) and integrate estimated read duration into blog post frontmatter, post header, and blog card previews. Display as "X min read" format to improve user experience and content transparency.
acceptanceCriteria: calculateReadingTime(content: string) function returns { minutes: number; words: number } using 200 wpm baseline (min 1 min); unit tests verify 1000-word content → 5 min and 500-word content → 3 min
Blog post cards display "X min read" badge in bottom-right corner; blog post header shows "By Author | Published Date | X min read" layout
BlogPost type includes readingTime: number field; all posts in site/src/data/blog/posts.ts have validated readingTime based on content length
technicalNotes: File to create: site/src/utils/reading-time.ts (~40 lines, export calculateReadingTime function)
File to edit: site/src/data/blog/posts.ts (add readingTime: number to BlogPost interface and populate for all posts)
File to edit: site/src/components/BlogPostCard.tsx (add {post.readingTime} min read)
Test command: npm run test -- reading-time.test.ts
Logic: const words = content.split(/\s+/).length; const minutes = Math.max(1, Math.ceil(words / 200))
